senses.definition: (countable) A single pass of a needle in sewing; the loop or turn of the thread thus made.

subsenses.definition: (medicine) A single pass of a surgical suture (to sew the edges of a wound together)
examples: I cut myself badly while cooking and needed to go to hospital to get stitches.

senses.definition: An arrangement of stitches in sewing, or method of stitching in some particular way or style.
(countable and uncountable) An intense stabbing pain under the lower edge of the ribcage, brought on by exercise or laughing.
examples: I've got a stitch. I'm going to have to stop and rest.
After about fifteen minutes I got terrible stitch.

senses.definition: A local sharp pain (anywhere); an acute pain, like the piercing of a needle.
examples: Violent continuous stitch in the region of the heart, the stitches multiplied when arresting the breathing. […] Feeling of heaviness in the muscles of the neck; he is obliged to bend his neck backwards. Cramp-like pain in right muscles of the neck, terminating in a stitch; the pain went off after motion and returned afterwards. […] Dull stitches in the region of the haunch-bones; pressure on the parts causes a simple pain. […] Drawing stitch in the right thigh, not perceptible when standing or ascending an elevation.
